title: Rav Chana of Baghdad
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: (Some read Rav Huna of Baghdad.) (The name Bagdata’ah, Rashi explains on Berakhot 54b and Ketubot 7b, and the Rashbam on Bava Batra 142b, is a town-name, namely Baghdad in Babylonia; in Yevamot 16a Rashi explains that he was a master of aggadah. Hyman suggests that possibly he means Sukkah 52b, where they said “with Chana of the aggadah, why do I need it?” — but there it refers to Rav Chana bar Bizna.) He was Shmuel’s student, as in Yevamot 67a, Ketubot 7b and Bava Batra 142b, where Shmuel said to him: “Go bring me ten [men], and I will tell you in their presence: One who grants ownership to a fetus — it acquires.” In Zevachim 92a Shmuel said to him: “… and I will tell you before them: Libations that became impure,” etc. Likewise we find “Rav Chana of Baghdad said that Shmuel said,” as in Shabbat 147b and 148a; in Eruvin 81b he said to Rav Yehudah, “Shmuel said: Even in an alley,” etc.; and in Berakhot 54b, when Rav Yehudah fell ill and recovered, Rav Chana of Baghdad and the Rabbis went in to him and said: “Blessed is the Merciful One, who gave you to us and did not give you to the dust.”

He was expert in the nature of fruits, as in Ketubot 10a, where he said: “Dates warm, satisfy, loosen, strengthen, and do not make delicate.” Hyman finds no surviving halakhot of his own, and he is mentioned only in Zevachim 9a, challenging: “But can you say so?” etc.

notes.text: Supplied Ketubot10a is retained; saved Davidson10b contains the dates saying. The Baghdad place-name versus aggadah interpretation and Huna/Chana variant remain attributed alternatives; Hyman’s own-halakhot negative is not a new exhaustive corpus search.

The consulted Ketubot 10b directly names Rav Chana Bagdataa and preserves the complete dates saying; the body keeps Hyman’s 10a locator. His place-name, aggadah and Huna/Chana alternatives, and his negative claim about surviving halakhot, are not independently settled by this one passage.
